**2018 in film** is an overview of events, including the highest-grossing films, award ceremonies, critics' lists of the best films of 2018, festivals, a list of films released, and notable deaths.

## Evaluation of the year

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2018_in_film&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Evaluation of the year")]

[Richard Brody](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Brody "Richard Brody") of _[The New Yorker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_New\_Yorker "The New Yorker")_ said,

> 2018 has been a banner year for movies, but you'd never know it from a trip to a local multiplex—or from a glimpse at the Oscarizables. The gap between what's good and what's widely available in theatres—between the cinema of resistance and the cinema of consensus—is wider than ever.

He also stated,

> In some cases, streaming has filled the gap. Several of the year's best movies, such _[Shirkers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shirkers "Shirkers")_ and _[The Ballad of Buster Scruggs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Ballad\_of\_Buster\_Scruggs "The Ballad of Buster Scruggs")_, are being released by [Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix") at the same time as (or just after) a limited theatrical run. Others, which barely qualified as having theatrical releases (one theatre for a week), are now available to stream online, on demand, and are more widely accessible to viewers (albeit at home) than films playing at thousands of multiplexes. Yet an impermanence, a threat of disappearance with the flick of a switch, hangs threateningly over independent films that are sent out on streaming.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_in_film#cite_note-1)

### 2018 box office records

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2018_in_film&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: 2018 box office records")]

*   The [Marvel Cinematic Universe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marvel_Cinematic_Universe "Marvel Cinematic Universe") became the [first film franchise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_highest-grossing_franchises_and_film_series "List of highest-grossing franchises and film series") to gross more than $14 billion with the release of _Black Panther_,[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_in_film#cite_note-3) and the first franchise to release five billion-dollar-grossing films (with _[Black Panther](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black\_Panther\_(film) "Black Panther (film)")_ joining _[The Avengers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Avengers\_(2012\_film) "The Avengers (2012 film)")_, _[Iron Man 3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iron\_Man\_3 "Iron Man 3")_, _[Avengers: Age of Ultron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avengers:\_Age\_of\_Ultron "Avengers: Age of Ultron")_, and _[Captain America: Civil War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Captain\_America:\_Civil\_War "Captain America: Civil War")_). Two months later, the MCU became the first film franchise to gross more than $15 billion and $16 billion with the release of _[Avengers: Infinity War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avengers:\_Infinity\_War "Avengers: Infinity War")_, which became the sixth billion-dollar-grossing film in the franchise,[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_in_film#cite_note-4) and also the first film in the franchise to earn $2 billion; and the MCU also became the first film franchise with two billion-dollar-grossing films released in the same year (with _Black Panther_ and _Avengers: Infinity War_). Two months after that, the MCU became the first film franchise to gross over $17 billion with the release of _[Ant-Man and the Wasp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ant-Man\_and\_the\_Wasp "Ant-Man and the Wasp")_.
*   [China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China "China") set an all-time biggest global one-month record in February with CN¥10.14 billion ($1.6 billion), calculating revenues from both local and foreign films. The record breaking number was largely attributed to the [Lunar New Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lunar_New_Year "Lunar New Year") holiday. The previous global monthly box office record was set in July 2011 in North America with $1.395 billion and the previous highest-grossing month in China was August 2017 with CN¥7.38 billion ($1.17 billion).[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_in_film#cite_note-5) The highest-grossing films in China during the month were the domestic films _[Operation Red Sea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation\_Red\_Sea "Operation Red Sea")_, _[Monster Hunt 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monster\_Hunt\_2 "Monster Hunt 2")_, and _[Detective Chinatown 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Detective\_Chinatown\_2 "Detective Chinatown 2")_, and the [Indian film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_film "Indian film")_[Secret Superstar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret\_Superstar "Secret Superstar")_.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_in_film#cite_note-6)
*   For the first time in history, February recorded $1 billion ticket sales in North America, fueled largely by the success of Disney/Marvel's _Black Panther_ which represented 43% or $428.8 million of the entire month's ticket sales. The previous February record was in 2012 with $818.4 million.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_in_film#cite_note-7)
*   In China, the combined opening weekend numbers of _Monster Hunt 2_ ($190 million), _Detective Chinatown 2_ ($154 million), _[The Monkey King 3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Monkey\_King\_3 "The Monkey King 3")_ ($79.9 million), _Operation Red Sea_ ($70.3 million) and _Boonie Bears: The Big Shrink_ ($40.9 million) amounted to a record breaking CN¥3.21 billion ($506 million) or $543 million weekend with online ticket sales, which is more than double the feat achieved in 2017 ($205 million) and 2016 ($224 million) during the same time period.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_in_film#cite_note-190M-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_in_film#cite_note-9) The previous weekend record was set in North America during the weekend of December 18–20, 2017, when the combined grosses of several films resulted in $306 million led by _[Star Wars: The Force Awakens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star\_Wars:\_The\_Force\_Awakens "Star Wars: The Force Awakens")_'$248 million debut.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_in_film#cite_note-506F-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_in_film#cite_note-11)
*   The same weekend, China also set a new [IMAX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMAX "IMAX") opening record when the combined IMAX earnings of the three films recorded $15.1 million, led by _Monster Hunt 2_ and _Detective Chinatown 2_ ($6.7 million).[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_in_film#cite_note-190M-8)
*   During the first quarter of 2018, China overtook North America as the world's largest box office market for the first time, with China grossing $3.17 billion compared to North America's $2.89 billion during that quarter.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_in_film#cite_note-12) Despite declining revenue from Hollywood films, Chinese box office growth was driven primarily by domestic Chinese films, led by _Operation Red Sea_ and _Detective Chinatown 2_, along with non-Hollywood foreign films, led by Indian [Bollywood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bollywood "Bollywood") films _[Secret Superstar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret\_Superstar "Secret Superstar")_ and _[Bajrangi Bhaijaan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bajrangi\_Bhaijaan "Bajrangi Bhaijaan")_.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_in_film#cite_note-13)

#### Film records

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2018_in_film&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Film records")]

*   _[Black Panther](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black\_Panther\_(film) "Black Panther (film)")_ grossed $202 million in its opening weekend and $242.16 million over the four-day holiday weekend, breaking the record for a February opening weekend and a [Presidents' Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington's_Birthday "Washington's Birthday") weekend, surpassing _[Deadpool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deadpool\_(film) "Deadpool (film)")_ ($132.4 million and $152.2 million in 2016), and recording the biggest opening weekend and total for a film directed by a [black](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Americans "African Americans") filmmaker, surpassing _[The Fate of the Furious](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Fate\_of\_the\_Furious "The Fate of the Furious")_ ($98.8 million by [F. Gary Gray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F._Gary_Gray "F. Gary Gray") in 2017). It also became just the fifth movie ever to gross more than $200 million [domestically](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_highest-grossing_openings_for_films#Biggest_openings_in_the_United_States_and_Canada "List of highest-grossing openings for films") in its opening weekend (joining _[The Avengers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Avengers\_(2012\_film) "The Avengers (2012 film)")_, _[Jurassic World](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jurassic\_World "Jurassic World")_, _[Star Wars: The Force Awakens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star\_Wars:\_The\_Force\_Awakens "Star Wars: The Force Awakens")_, and _[Star Wars: The Last Jedi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star\_Wars:\_The\_Last\_Jedi "Star Wars: The Last Jedi")_). On Monday, February 19, the film grossed another $40.17 million, breaking the record for a Monday gross and surpassing _Force Awakens_ ($40.11 million on December 21, 2015).[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_in_film#cite_note-hollywoodreporter-14) The subsequent $242.16 million four-day opening weekend became the second-biggest four-day gross ever, only behind _The Force Awakens'_ $288.07 million. On February 23–25, the film grossed another $111.7 million, recording the second-biggest second weekend gross behind _The Force Awakens_ ($149.2 million on December 25–27, 2015) and becoming just the fourth film to gross more than $100 million in its second weekend (joining _The Avengers_, _Jurassic World_, and _The Force Awakens_).[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_in_film#cite_note-15) On February 27, the film became the first superhero origin film and the tenth film overall to gross $500 million domestically (doing so in 17 days, the third fastest film to reach the milestone behind _The_ _Force Awakens_ and _The_ _Last Jedi_), surpassing _[Wonder Woman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wonder\_Woman\_(2017\_film) "Wonder Woman (2017 film)")_ ($412.6 million in 2017) to become the highest-grossing single character superhero origin film;[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_in_film#cite_note-comicbook-16) on March 9, the film reached $549.2 million domestically, surpassing _[The Dark Knight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Dark\_Knight "The Dark Knight")_ to become the highest grossing solo superhero film of all time. On March 16, the film became the seventh film to gross $600 million domestically (doing so in 31 days, the second fastest film to reach the milestone behind _The Force Awakens_), and just the second superhero movie to do so (along with _Avengers_). On March 24, the film reached a total domestic gross of $626 million to become the highest grossing superhero movie of all time, surpassing _The Avengers_ ($623.4 million in 2012). On March 30, the film became the fifth film to gross $650 million domestically (doing so in 45 days, the second fastest film to reach the milestone behind _Force Awakens_). On April 7, it reached a total domestic gross of $663.2 million to surpass _[Titanic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Titanic\_(1997\_film) "Titanic (1997 film)")_ as the [third-highest-grossing film in the United States and Canada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_highest-grossing_films_in_the_United_States_and_Canada "List of highest-grossing films in the United States and Canada"). On August 3, it reached a total domestic gross of $700 million, becoming the third film to reach the mark.
*   Black Panther also became the highest-grossing film of all time in West and East Africa, and the southern Africa region.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_in_film#cite_note-DeadlineIntWknd3-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_in_film#cite_note-AfricaRecord-18)
*   On March 9–12, Ryan Coogler's _Black Panther_ retained the #1 box office spot with a $40.8 million fourth weekend (the fourth biggest, behind _[American Sniper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American\_Sniper "American Sniper")_, _[Avatar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avatar\_(2009\_film) "Avatar (2009 film)")_, and _The Force Awakens_), while [Ava DuVernay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ava_DuVernay "Ava DuVernay")'s _[A Wrinkle in Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A\_Wrinkle\_in\_Time\_(2018\_film) "A Wrinkle in Time (2018 film)")_ opened at the #2 spot with a $33.1 million debut, marking the first time in history that the top two spots of a weekend were both held by [black](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_American "African American") directors.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_in_film#cite_note-19)
*   _[Avengers: Infinity War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avengers:\_Infinity\_War "Avengers: Infinity War")_ grossed $258 million in its opening weekend, breaking the record for biggest domestic opening weekend and surpassing _The Force Awakens_ ($248 million in [2015](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_in_film "2015 in film")). The film grossed $641 million worldwide opening weekend, becoming the first film ever to open with more than $600 million globally and surpassing _[The Fate of the Furious](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Fate\_of\_the\_Furious "The Fate of the Furious")_ ($542 million in [2017](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_in_film "2017 in film")). On April 27, the film grossed $106 million in its opening day, the second-highest single day gross behind _The Force Awakens_ ($119 million in [2015](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_in_film "2015 in film")) to become just the third movie ever to gross more than $100 million in a single day (joining _The Force Awakens_ and _The Last Jedi_); on April 28, the film grossed another $83 million, breaking the record for a Saturday gross and surpassing _[Jurassic World](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jurassic\_World "Jurassic World")_ ($69.6 million on 13 June 2015); on April 29, the film grossed another $69.2 million, breaking the record for a Sunday gross and surpassing _The Force Awakens_ ($60.5 million on 20 December 2015). The film became the second film of the decade to gross $2 billion, making the [2010s](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010s_in_film "2010s in film") the first decade to have two films gross $2 billion.
*   _[Bohemian Rhapsody](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bohemian\_Rhapsody\_(film) "Bohemian Rhapsody (film)")_, based on the life of [Queen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_(band) "Queen (band)")'s lead vocalist [Freddie Mercury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freddie_Mercury "Freddie Mercury"), grossed over $911 million worldwide,[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_in_film#cite_note-20) setting all-time records for the highest-grossing [biopic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biopic "Biopic") ever,[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_in_film#cite_note-Spanos-21)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_in_film#cite_note-movieweb-22)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_in_film#cite_note-indianexpress-23) the [highest-grossing musical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_highest-grossing_musicals "List of highest-grossing musicals") biopic,[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_in_film#cite_note-mendelson-24) and the highest-grossing [drama film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drama_film "Drama film") (without any action or fantasy).[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_in_film#cite_note-forbes-25)
*   _[Secret Superstar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret\_Superstar "Secret Superstar")_, an [Indian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cinema_of_India "Cinema of India")[musical drama film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Musical_drama_film "Musical drama film") that had its China release in January 2018, grossed $29.2 million in its opening weekend there,[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_in_film#cite_note-26) setting a record for an Indian film in China, surpassing _[Dangal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dangal\_(2016\_film) "Dangal (2016 film)")_; [Bollywood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bollywood "Bollywood") superstar [Aamir Khan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aamir_Khan "Aamir Khan") produced and starred in both films.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_in_film#cite_note-27)_Secret Superstar_'s first-week gross in China was $47 million,[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_in_film#cite_note-28) also a record for an Indian film in the country, again surpassing _Dangal_.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_in_film#cite_note-scmp-29)_Secret Superstar_ was the fourth highest-grossing foreign film in China during January–April 2018.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_in_film#cite_note-30)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_in_film#cite_note-31)_Secret Superstar_ also became one of the most profitable films of all time,[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_in_film#cite_note-medium-32)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_in_film#cite_note-bloomberg-ren-33)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_in_film#cite_note-washingtonpost-34)[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_in_film#cite_note-boi-35) grossing [₹](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_rupee "Indian rupee")9.65 billion[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_in_film#cite_note-:1-36) ($154 million)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_in_film#cite_note-statista-37) worldwide on a [limited budget](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Low-budget_film "Low-budget film") of ₹150 million (US$1.6 million), with over 6,000% [return on investment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Return_on_investment "Return on investment") (ROI).[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_in_film#cite_note-medium-32)[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_in_film#cite_note-bollywoodlife3-38)
*   _[Incredibles 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Incredibles\_2 "Incredibles 2")_ grossed $182.7 million domestically and $235.8 million worldwide in its opening weekend, setting records for the biggest domestic opening weekend for both Pixar and any animated film (surpassing _[Finding Dory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Finding\_Dory "Finding Dory")_, with $135.1 million in [2016](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_in_film "2016 in film")), the biggest worldwide opening for Pixar (surpassing _Finding Dory_), and the [biggest opening weekend worldwide for an animated film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_highest-grossing_openings_for_animated_films "List of highest-grossing openings for animated films") (surpassing _[Ice Age: Dawn of the Dinosaurs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ice\_Age:\_Dawn\_of\_the\_Dinosaurs "Ice Age: Dawn of the Dinosaurs")_, with $218.4 million in [2009](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_in_film "2009 in film")). It also set the record for the biggest opening for a PG rated movie (surpassing _[Beauty and the Beast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beauty\_and\_the\_Beast\_(2017\_film) "Beauty and the Beast (2017 film)")_ with $174.8 million in [2017](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_in_film "2017 in film")). It became the first animated film to earn $500 million at the domestic box office, later the first animated film to earn $600 million at the domestic box office, earning just over $602 million and surpassing the previous record set by _Finding Dory_ by over $100 million.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_in_film#cite_note-39) It is also the fastest animated film to gross $1 billion worldwide doing so in 46 days, surpassing _[Minions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minions\_(film) "Minions (film)")_ (49 days).[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]
*   _[Bohemian Rhapsody](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bohemian\_Rhapsody\_(film) "Bohemian Rhapsody (film)")_ became the [Highest grossing biographical films](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_biographical_films "List of biographical films") surpassing _[The Passion of the Christ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Passion\_of\_the\_Christ "The Passion of the Christ")_.

## Evaluation of the year

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2018_in_film&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Evaluation of the year")]

[Richard Brody](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Brody "Richard Brody") of _[The New Yorker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_New\_Yorker "The New Yorker")_ said,

> 2018 has been a banner year for movies, but you'd never know it from a trip to a local multiplex—or from a glimpse at the Oscarizables. The gap between what's good and what's widely available in theatres—between the cinema of resistance and the cinema of consensus—is wider than ever.

He also stated,

> In some cases, streaming has filled the gap. Several of the year's best movies, such _[Shirkers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shirkers "Shirkers")_ and _[The Ballad of Buster Scruggs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Ballad\_of\_Buster\_Scruggs "The Ballad of Buster Scruggs")_, are being released by [Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix") at the same time as (or just after) a limited theatrical run. Others, which barely qualified as having theatrical releases (one theatre for a week), are now available to stream online, on demand, and are more widely accessible to viewers (albeit at home) than films playing at thousands of multiplexes. Yet an impermanence, a threat of disappearance with the flick of a switch, hangs threateningly over independent films that are sent out on streaming.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_in_film#cite_note-1)

### 2018 box office records

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2018_in_film&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: 2018 box office records")]

*   The [Marvel Cinematic Universe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marvel_Cinematic_Universe "Marvel Cinematic Universe") became the [first film franchise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_highest-grossing_franchises_and_film_series "List of highest-grossing franchises and film series") to gross more than $14 billion with the release of _Black Panther_,[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_in_film#cite_note-3) and the first franchise to release five billion-dollar-grossing films (with _[Black Panther](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black\_Panther\_(film) "Black Panther (film)")_ joining _[The Avengers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Avengers\_(2012\_film) "The Avengers (2012 film)")_, _[Iron Man 3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iron\_Man\_3 "Iron Man 3")_, _[Avengers: Age of Ultron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avengers:\_Age\_of\_Ultron "Avengers: Age of Ultron")_, and _[Captain America: Civil War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Captain\_America:\_Civil\_War "Captain America: Civil War")_). Two months later, the MCU became the first film franchise to gross more than $15 billion and $16 billion with the release of _[Avengers: Infinity War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avengers:\_Infinity\_War "Avengers: Infinity War")_, which became the sixth billion-dollar-grossing film in the franchise,[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_in_film#cite_note-4) and also the first film in the franchise to earn $2 billion; and the MCU also became the first film franchise with two billion-dollar-grossing films released in the same year (with _Black Panther_ and _Avengers: Infinity War_). Two months after that, the MCU became the first film franchise to gross over $17 billion with the release of _[Ant-Man and the Wasp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ant-Man\_and\_the\_Wasp "Ant-Man and the Wasp")_.
*   [China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China "China") set an all-time biggest global one-month record in February with CN¥10.14 billion ($1.6 billion), calculating revenues from both local and foreign films. The record breaking number was largely attributed to the [Lunar New Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lunar_New_Year "Lunar New Year") holiday. The previous global monthly box office record was set in July 2011 in North America with $1.395 billion and the previous highest-grossing month in China was August 2017 with CN¥7.38 billion ($1.17 billion).[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_in_film#cite_note-5) The highest-grossing films in China during the month were the domestic films _[Operation Red Sea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation\_Red\_Sea "Operation Red Sea")_, _[Monster Hunt 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monster\_Hunt\_2 "Monster Hunt 2")_, and _[Detective Chinatown 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Detective\_Chinatown\_2 "Detective Chinatown 2")_, and the [Indian film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_film "Indian film")_[Secret Superstar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret\_Superstar "Secret Superstar")_.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_in_film#cite_note-6)
*   For the first time in history, February recorded $1 billion ticket sales in North America, fueled largely by the success of Disney/Marvel's _Black Panther_ which represented 43% or $428.8 million of the entire month's ticket sales. The previous February record was in 2012 with $818.4 million.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_in_film#cite_note-7)
*   In China, the combined opening weekend numbers of _Monster Hunt 2_ ($190 million), _Detective Chinatown 2_ ($154 million), _[The Monkey King 3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Monkey\_King\_3 "The Monkey King 3")_ ($79.9 million), _Operation Red Sea_ ($70.3 million) and _Boonie Bears: The Big Shrink_ ($40.9 million) amounted to a record breaking CN¥3.21 billion ($506 million) or $543 million weekend with online ticket sales, which is more than double the feat achieved in 2017 ($205 million) and 2016 ($224 million) during the same time period.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_in_film#cite_note-190M-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_in_film#cite_note-9) The previous weekend record was set in North America during the weekend of December 18–20, 2017, when the combined grosses of several films resulted in $306 million led by _[Star Wars: The Force Awakens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star\_Wars:\_The\_Force\_Awakens "Star Wars: The Force Awakens")_'$248 million debut.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_in_film#cite_note-506F-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_in_film#cite_note-11)
*   The same weekend, China also set a new [IMAX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMAX "IMAX") opening record when the combined IMAX earnings of the three films recorded $15.1 million, led by _Monster Hunt 2_ and _Detective Chinatown 2_ ($6.7 million).[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_in_film#cite_note-190M-8)
*   During the first quarter of 2018, China overtook North America as the world's largest box office market for the first time, with China grossing $3.17 billion compared to North America's $2.89 billion during that quarter.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_in_film#cite_note-12) Despite declining revenue from Hollywood films, Chinese box office growth was driven primarily by domestic Chinese films, led by _Operation Red Sea_ and _Detective Chinatown 2_, along with non-Hollywood foreign films, led by Indian [Bollywood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bollywood "Bollywood") films _[Secret Superstar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret\_Superstar "Secret Superstar")_ and _[Bajrangi Bhaijaan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bajrangi\_Bhaijaan "Bajrangi Bhaijaan")_.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_in_film#cite_note-13)

#### Studio records

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2018_in_film&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Studio records")]

*   [Walt Disney Studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walt_Disney_Studios_(division) "Walt Disney Studios (division)") became the fastest studio ever to reach $1 billion for the year at the domestic box office; it reached this goal in 117 days on April 27, 2018, beating its own record of 128 days set on May 7, 2016. 
    *   Walt Disney Studios also grossed over $7 billion worldwide and $3 billion domestic, making it its 2nd time after [2016](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_in_film "2016 in film"). It passed Disney's 2016 domestic gross and it's in 2nd place this year.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

*   With _Incredibles 2_, [Pixar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pixar "Pixar") became the first animation studio to have three animated films (_[Toy Story 3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toy\_Story\_3 "Toy Story 3")_, _[Finding Dory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Finding\_Dory "Finding Dory")_) each surpass $1 billion at the worldwide box office.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

#### Film records

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2018_in_film&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Film records")]

*   _[Black Panther](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black\_Panther\_(film) "Black Panther (film)")_ grossed $202 million in its opening weekend and $242.16 million over the four-day holiday weekend, breaking the record for a February opening weekend and a [Presidents' Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington's_Birthday "Washington's Birthday") weekend, surpassing _[Deadpool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deadpool\_(film) "Deadpool (film)")_ ($132.4 million and $152.2 million in 2016), and recording the biggest opening weekend and total for a film directed by a [black](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Americans "African Americans") filmmaker, surpassing _[The Fate of the Furious](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Fate\_of\_the\_Furious "The Fate of the Furious")_ ($98.8 million by [F. Gary Gray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F._Gary_Gray "F. Gary Gray") in 2017). It also became just the fifth movie ever to gross more than $200 million [domestically](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_highest-grossing_openings_for_films#Biggest_openings_in_the_United_States_and_Canada "List of highest-grossing openings for films") in its opening weekend (joining _[The Avengers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Avengers\_(2012\_film) "The Avengers (2012 film)")_, _[Jurassic World](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jurassic\_World "Jurassic World")_, _[Star Wars: The Force Awakens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star\_Wars:\_The\_Force\_Awakens "Star Wars: The Force Awakens")_, and _[Star Wars: The Last Jedi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star\_Wars:\_The\_Last\_Jedi "Star Wars: The Last Jedi")_). On Monday, February 19, the film grossed another $40.17 million, breaking the record for a Monday gross and surpassing _Force Awakens_ ($40.11 million on December 21, 2015).[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_in_film#cite_note-hollywoodreporter-14) The subsequent $242.16 million four-day opening weekend became the second-biggest four-day gross ever, only behind _The Force Awakens'_ $288.07 million. On February 23–25, the film grossed another $111.7 million, recording the second-biggest second weekend gross behind _The Force Awakens_ ($149.2 million on December 25–27, 2015) and becoming just the fourth film to gross more than $100 million in its second weekend (joining _The Avengers_, _Jurassic World_, and _The Force Awakens_).[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_in_film#cite_note-15) On February 27, the film became the first superhero origin film and the tenth film overall to gross $500 million domestically (doing so in 17 days, the third fastest film to reach the milestone behind _The_ _Force Awakens_ and _The_ _Last Jedi_), surpassing _[Wonder Woman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wonder\_Woman\_(2017\_film) "Wonder Woman (2017 film)")_ ($412.6 million in 2017) to become the highest-grossing single character superhero origin film;[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_in_film#cite_note-comicbook-16) on March 9, the film reached $549.2 million domestically, surpassing _[The Dark Knight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Dark\_Knight "The Dark Knight")_ to become the highest grossing solo superhero film of all time. On March 16, the film became the seventh film to gross $600 million domestically (doing so in 31 days, the second fastest film to reach the milestone behind _The Force Awakens_), and just the second superhero movie to do so (along with _Avengers_). On March 24, the film reached a total domestic gross of $626 million to become the highest grossing superhero movie of all time, surpassing _The Avengers_ ($623.4 million in 2012). On March 30, the film became the fifth film to gross $650 million domestically (doing so in 45 days, the second fastest film to reach the milestone behind _Force Awakens_). On April 7, it reached a total domestic gross of $663.2 million to surpass _[Titanic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Titanic\_(1997\_film) "Titanic (1997 film)")_ as the [third-highest-grossing film in the United States and Canada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_highest-grossing_films_in_the_United_States_and_Canada "List of highest-grossing films in the United States and Canada"). On August 3, it reached a total domestic gross of $700 million, becoming the third film to reach the mark.
*   Black Panther also became the highest-grossing film of all time in West and East Africa, and the southern Africa region.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_in_film#cite_note-DeadlineIntWknd3-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_in_film#cite_note-AfricaRecord-18)
*   On March 9–12, Ryan Coogler's _Black Panther_ retained the #1 box office spot with a $40.8 million fourth weekend (the fourth biggest, behind _[American Sniper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American\_Sniper "American Sniper")_, _[Avatar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avatar\_(2009\_film) "Avatar (2009 film)")_, and _The Force Awakens_), while [Ava DuVernay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ava_DuVernay "Ava DuVernay")'s _[A Wrinkle in Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A\_Wrinkle\_in\_Time\_(2018\_film) "A Wrinkle in Time (2018 film)")_ opened at the #2 spot with a $33.1 million debut, marking the first time in history that the top two spots of a weekend were both held by [black](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_American "African American") directors.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_in_film#cite_note-19)
*   _[Avengers: Infinity War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avengers:\_Infinity\_War "Avengers: Infinity War")_ grossed $258 million in its opening weekend, breaking the record for biggest domestic opening weekend and surpassing _The Force Awakens_ ($248 million in [2015](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_in_film "2015 in film")). The film grossed $641 million worldwide opening weekend, becoming the first film ever to open with more than $600 million globally and surpassing _[The Fate of the Furious](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Fate\_of\_the\_Furious "The Fate of the Furious")_ ($542 million in [2017](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_in_film "2017 in film")). On April 27, the film grossed $106 million in its opening day, the second-highest single day gross behind _The Force Awakens_ ($119 million in [2015](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_in_film "2015 in film")) to become just the third movie ever to gross more than $100 million in a single day (joining _The Force Awakens_ and _The Last Jedi_); on April 28, the film grossed another $83 million, breaking the record for a Saturday gross and surpassing _[Jurassic World](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jurassic\_World "Jurassic World")_ ($69.6 million on 13 June 2015); on April 29, the film grossed another $69.2 million, breaking the record for a Sunday gross and surpassing _The Force Awakens_ ($60.5 million on 20 December 2015). The film became the second film of the decade to gross $2 billion, making the [2010s](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010s_in_film "2010s in film") the first decade to have two films gross $2 billion.
*   _[Bohemian Rhapsody](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bohemian\_Rhapsody\_(film) "Bohemian Rhapsody (film)")_, based on the life of [Queen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_(band) "Queen (band)")'s lead vocalist [Freddie Mercury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freddie_Mercury "Freddie Mercury"), grossed over $911 million worldwide,[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_in_film#cite_note-20) setting all-time records for the highest-grossing [biopic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biopic "Biopic") ever,[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_in_film#cite_note-Spanos-21)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_in_film#cite_note-movieweb-22)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_in_film#cite_note-indianexpress-23) the [highest-grossing musical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_highest-grossing_musicals "List of highest-grossing musicals") biopic,[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_in_film#cite_note-mendelson-24) and the highest-grossing [drama film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drama_film "Drama film") (without any action or fantasy).[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_in_film#cite_note-forbes-25)
*   _[Secret Superstar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret\_Superstar "Secret Superstar")_, an [Indian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cinema_of_India "Cinema of India")[musical drama film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Musical_drama_film "Musical drama film") that had its China release in January 2018, grossed $29.2 million in its opening weekend there,[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_in_film#cite_note-26) setting a record for an Indian film in China, surpassing _[Dangal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dangal\_(2016\_film) "Dangal (2016 film)")_; [Bollywood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bollywood "Bollywood") superstar [Aamir Khan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aamir_Khan "Aamir Khan") produced and starred in both films.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_in_film#cite_note-27)_Secret Superstar_'s first-week gross in China was $47 million,[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_in_film#cite_note-28) also a record for an Indian film in the country, again surpassing _Dangal_.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_in_film#cite_note-scmp-29)_Secret Superstar_ was the fourth highest-grossing foreign film in China during January–April 2018.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_in_film#cite_note-30)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_in_film#cite_note-31)_Secret Superstar_ also became one of the most profitable films of all time,[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_in_film#cite_note-medium-32)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_in_film#cite_note-bloomberg-ren-33)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_in_film#cite_note-washingtonpost-34)[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_in_film#cite_note-boi-35) grossing [₹](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_rupee "Indian rupee")9.65 billion[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_in_film#cite_note-:1-36) ($154 million)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_in_film#cite_note-statista-37) worldwide on a [limited budget](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Low-budget_film "Low-budget film") of ₹150 million (US$1.6 million), with over 6,000% [return on investment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Return_on_investment "Return on investment") (ROI).[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_in_film#cite_note-medium-32)[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_in_film#cite_note-bollywoodlife3-38)
*   _[Incredibles 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Incredibles\_2 "Incredibles 2")_ grossed $182.7 million domestically and $235.8 million worldwide in its opening weekend, setting records for the biggest domestic opening weekend for both Pixar and any animated film (surpassing _[Finding Dory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Finding\_Dory "Finding Dory")_, with $135.1 million in [2016](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_in_film "2016 in film")), the biggest worldwide opening for Pixar (surpassing _Finding Dory_), and the [biggest opening weekend worldwide for an animated film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_highest-grossing_openings_for_animated_films "List of highest-grossing openings for animated films") (surpassing _[Ice Age: Dawn of the Dinosaurs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ice\_Age:\_Dawn\_of\_the\_Dinosaurs "Ice Age: Dawn of the Dinosaurs")_, with $218.4 million in [2009](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_in_film "2009 in film")). It also set the record for the biggest opening for a PG rated movie (surpassing _[Beauty and the Beast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beauty\_and\_the\_Beast\_(2017\_film) "Beauty and the Beast (2017 film)")_ with $174.8 million in [2017](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_in_film "2017 in film")). It became the first animated film to earn $500 million at the domestic box office, later the first animated film to earn $600 million at the domestic box office, earning just over $602 million and surpassing the previous record set by _Finding Dory_ by over $100 million.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_in_film#cite_note-39) It is also the fastest animated film to gross $1 billion worldwide doing so in 46 days, surpassing _[Minions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minions\_(film) "Minions (film)")_ (49 days).[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]
*   _[Bohemian Rhapsody](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bohemian\_Rhapsody\_(film) "Bohemian Rhapsody (film)")_ became the [Highest grossing biographical films](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_biographical_films "List of biographical films") surpassing _[The Passion of the Christ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Passion\_of\_the\_Christ "The Passion of the Christ")_.

**2016 in film** is an overview of events, including the highest-grossing films, award ceremonies, festivals, a list of films released, and notable deaths.

## Evaluation of the year

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2016_in_film&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Evaluation of the year")]

In his article highlighting the best films of 2016, [Richard Brody](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Brody "Richard Brody") of _[The New Yorker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_New\_Yorker "The New Yorker")_ stated,

> Hollywood is the world's best money-laundering machine. It takes in huge amounts of money from the sale of mass-market commodities and cleanses some of it with the production of cinematic masterworks. Earning billions of dollars from C.G.I. comedies for children, superhero movies, sci-fi apocalypses, and other popular genres, the big studios channel some of those funds into movies by [Wes Anderson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wes_Anderson "Wes Anderson"), [Sofia Coppola](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sofia_Coppola "Sofia Coppola"), [Spike Lee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spike_Lee "Spike Lee"), [Martin Scorsese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martin_Scorsese "Martin Scorsese"), [James Gray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Gray_(director) "James Gray (director)"), and other worthies. Sometimes there's even an overlap between the two groups of movies, as when [Ryan Coogler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryan_Coogler "Ryan Coogler") made _[Creed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Creed\_(film) "Creed (film)")_, or when Scorsese made the modernist horror instant-classic _[Shutter Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shutter\_Island\_(film) "Shutter Island (film)")_, or when [Clint Eastwood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clint_Eastwood "Clint Eastwood") makes just about anything.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_in_film#cite_note-1)

_[Captain America: Civil War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Captain\_America:\_Civil\_War "Captain America: Civil War")_, _[Rogue One: A Star Wars Story](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rogue\_One "Rogue One")_, _[Finding Dory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Finding\_Dory "Finding Dory")_, and _[Zootopia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zootopia "Zootopia")_ grossed more than $1 billion each, making them among the [highest-grossing films of all time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_highest-grossing_films "List of highest-grossing films"). This is the first year that two animated films (_Finding Dory_ and _Zootopia_) grossed over $1 billion in a single year, and are among the [highest-grossing animated films](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_highest-grossing_animated_films "List of highest-grossing animated films").

_Captain America: Civil War_, _Zootopia_, _[Kung Fu Panda 3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kung\_Fu\_Panda\_3 "Kung Fu Panda 3")_, _[Warcraft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warcraft\_(film) "Warcraft (film)")_, and _[The Great Wall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Great\_Wall\_(2016\_film) "The Great Wall (2016 film)")_ have all grossed more than [¥](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renminbi "Renminbi")1 billion at the [Chinese box office](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_highest-grossing_films_in_China "List of highest-grossing films in China"), making them among the highest-grossing films in China.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_in_film#cite_note-3)

### 2016 box office records

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2016_in_film&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: 2016 box office records")]

#### Studio records

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2016_in_film&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Studio records")]

*   [Walt Disney Studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walt_Disney_Studios_(division) "Walt Disney Studios (division)") reached $1 billion at the domestic box office faster than any other studio; it reached this goal on the 128th day of 2016, beating [Universal Studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universal_Pictures "Universal Pictures")' record of reaching the goal on the 165th day of [2015](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_in_film "2015 in film").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_in_film#cite_note-4) Disney's previous record for reaching $1 billion was on the 174th day of 2015. The studio became the first to have five of its releases (_[Rogue One](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rogue\_One "Rogue One")_, _[Finding Dory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Finding\_Dory "Finding Dory")_, _[Captain America: Civil War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Captain\_America:\_Civil\_War "Captain America: Civil War")_, _[The Jungle Book](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Jungle\_Book\_(2016\_film) "The Jungle Book (2016 film)")_, and _[Zootopia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zootopia "Zootopia")_) from a single year reach $300 million domestically. Disney also eclipsed Universal's 2015 record for most films from a single year crossing $1 billion worldwide with four (_Captain America: Civil War_, _Rogue One_, _Finding Dory_, and _Zootopia_), setting a new record for most billion-dollar-grossing films over two years with six (including _[Avengers: Age of Ultron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avengers:\_Age\_of\_Ultron "Avengers: Age of Ultron")_ and _[Star Wars: The Force Awakens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star\_Wars:\_The\_Force\_Awakens "Star Wars: The Force Awakens")_). Walt Disney Studios has also become the first studio to have the five highest-grossing films worldwide,[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_in_film#cite_note-5) and the first since at least 1913 to have the three highest-grossing films in the U.S., both in a single year. Disney became the first studio to gross more than $3 billion at the domestic box office and, with the release of _Rogue One_, became the first to gross more than $7 billion at the global box office, surpassing Universal's previous record of $6.9 billion in 2015.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_in_film#cite_note-6) Disney later passes $7 billion at the global box office again in 2018. Disney is also the first studio to have three films gross over $400 million domestically in a single year (_Rogue One_, _Finding Dory_, and _Captain America: Civil War_), and the first to fill in all slots of the top five films of any particular year.
*   Disney's [Marvel Cinematic Universe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marvel_Cinematic_Universe "Marvel Cinematic Universe") became the first film franchise to have four of its films gross over $1 billion with _Captain America: Civil War_ joining [2012](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_in_film "2012 in film")'s _[The Avengers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Avengers\_(2012\_film) "The Avengers (2012 film)")_, [2013](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_in_film "2013 in film")'s _[Iron Man 3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iron\_Man\_3 "Iron Man 3")_ and 2015's _Avengers: Age of Ultron_, and the first to gross more than $10 billion with the release of _Civil War_.

#### Film records

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2016_in_film&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Film records")]

*   _[Deadpool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deadpool\_(film) "Deadpool (film)")_ became the second-highest-grossing R-rated domestic film of all time with $363.1 million, after _[The Passion of the Christ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Passion\_of\_the\_Christ "The Passion of the Christ")_ ($370.8 million in [2004](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_in_film "2004 in film")). It later became the highest-grossing R-rated film of all time worldwide, surpassing _[The Matrix Reloaded](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Matrix\_Reloaded "The Matrix Reloaded")_, with $783.1 million. It also became the highest-grossing superhero film not to feature [Batman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Batman "Batman"), [Spider-Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spider-Man "Spider-Man"), or [Iron Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iron_Man "Iron Man") in any capacity.
*   _[Zootopia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zootopia "Zootopia")_ became the highest-grossing original animated film of all time, surpassing _[Finding Nemo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Finding\_Nemo "Finding Nemo")_ ($940.3 million in [2003](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2003_in_film "2003 in film")). Along with _[Finding Dory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Finding\_Dory "Finding Dory")_, it became one of two animated films to earn over $1 billion in the same year, a first.
*   _[Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Batman\_v\_Superman:\_Dawn\_of\_Justice "Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice")_ had the biggest worldwide opening weekend ever for a superhero film with $422.5 million, surpassing _The Avengers_ ($392.5 million in 2012). The film, along with _Captain America: Civil War_, were the most expensive films of the year ($250 million).
*   _[Dangal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dangal\_(2016\_film) "Dangal (2016 film)")_ became the highest-grossing [Indian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cinema_of_India "Cinema of India") film of all-time, partly due to successful ticket-sales in [China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China "China").
*   _[The Mermaid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Mermaid\_(2016\_film) "The Mermaid (2016 film)")_ became the [highest-grossing film ever in China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_highest-grossing_films_in_China "List of highest-grossing films in China") and the first film ever to earn over $500 million without a wide North American release.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_in_film#cite_note-7)
*   _[Shin Godzilla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shin\_Godzilla "Shin Godzilla")_, the 31st Godzilla film, grossed about ¥82.5 billion ($77.9 million), making it the highest-grossing Japanese-made film in the franchise, the most successful live-action Japanese film in 2016, and the second-most successful film of the year in Japan.
*   The [anime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anime "Anime") film _[Your Name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Your\_Name "Your Name")_ grossed US$354 million,[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_in_film#cite_note-8) becoming the [highest-grossing anime film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_highest-grossing_anime_films "List of highest-grossing anime films"), the [fourth-highest-grossing film in Japan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_highest-grossing_films_in_Japan "List of highest-grossing films in Japan"), and the [seventh-highest-grossing traditionally animated film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_highest-grossing_animated_films#Traditional_animation "List of highest-grossing animated films"). In [China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China "China"), it grossed US$81.3 million, becoming the highest-grossing 2D animated film[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_in_film#cite_note-9) and the highest-grossing Japanese film in the world's second-largest movie market,[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_in_film#cite_note-10) as well as the highest-grossing non-Hollywood foreign film in China until it was surpassed by Indian film _[Dangal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dangal\_(2016\_film) "Dangal (2016 film)")_.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_in_film#cite_note-usnews-11)
*   _[Warcraft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warcraft\_(film) "Warcraft (film)")_ became the highest-grossing [video game adaptation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_films_based_on_video_games "List of films based on video games") worldwide, with $433.5 million,[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_in_film#cite_note-12) surpassing _[Prince of Persia: The Sands of Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prince\_of\_Persia:\_The\_Sands\_of\_Time\_(film) "Prince of Persia: The Sands of Time (film)")_ ($336.4 million in [2010](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_in_film "2010 in film")).
*   _Finding Dory_ grossed $135.1 million domestically and $185.7 million worldwide in its opening weekend, setting records for the biggest domestic opening weekend for both Pixar (surpassing _[Toy Story 3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toy\_Story\_3 "Toy Story 3")_, with $110.3 million in 2010) and any animated film (surpassing _[Shrek the Third](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shrek\_the\_Third "Shrek the Third")_, with $121.6 million in [2007](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_in_film "2007 in film")), the biggest worldwide opening weekend for Pixar (surpassing _[Inside Out](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inside\_Out "Inside Out")_, with $180.1 million in 2015), and the second-biggest opening weekend worldwide for an animated film after _[Ice Age: Dawn of the Dinosaurs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ice\_Age:\_Dawn\_of\_the\_Dinosaurs "Ice Age: Dawn of the Dinosaurs")_ ($218.4 million in [2009](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_in_film "2009 in film")). It later became the highest-grossing animated film at the domestic box office, surpassing _[Shrek 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shrek\_2 "Shrek 2")_ ($441.2 million in 2004). It became the first animated film to cross $450, $460, $470, and $480 million at the domestic box office. Along with _Zootopia_, it became one of two animated films to earn over $1 billion in the same year, a first. It also became the eighth film to do so during the two-year period of 2015–16, surpassing the previous record of seven billion-dollar films during the two-year period of 2011–12.
*   _[The Secret Life of Pets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Secret\_Life\_of\_Pets "The Secret Life of Pets")_ grossed $104.4 million domestically in its opening weekend, breaking _Inside Out_'s record ($90.4 million) for the highest domestic opening weekend for an original film of any kind, and became the first original film to open above $100 million domestically. It also became the highest-grossing original non-Disney animated film ever, both domestically (surpassing _[Despicable Me](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Despicable\_Me "Despicable Me")_, with $251.5 million in 2010) and worldwide (beating _[Kung Fu Panda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kung\_Fu\_Panda\_(film) "Kung Fu Panda (film)")_, with $631.7 million in [2008](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_in_film "2008 in film")).
*   _[Sausage Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sausage\_Party "Sausage Party")_ became the highest-grossing R-rated animated film of all time ($140.7 million), surpassing _[South Park: Bigger, Longer & Uncut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South\_Park:\_Bigger,\_Longer\_&\_Uncut "South Park: Bigger, Longer & Uncut")_ ($83.1 million in 1999).
*   _[Doctor Strange](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor\_Strange\_(2016\_film) "Doctor Strange (2016 film)")_ became the highest-grossing single-character debut of any Marvel Cinematic Universe film worldwide with $677.7 million, beating _[Iron Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iron\_Man\_(2008\_film) "Iron Man (2008 film)")_ ($585.2 million in 2008).
*   2016 became the first year to have ten films to cross $700 million worldwide, beating 2014's record of nine films. It also surpassed the latter year in terms of most films earning more than $500 million with sixteen (_Doctor Strange_, _[Moana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana\_(2016\_film) "Moana (2016 film)")_, _[Sing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sing\_(2016\_American\_film) "Sing (2016 American film)")_, _The Mermaid_, _[X-Men: Apocalypse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/X-Men:\_Apocalypse "X-Men: Apocalypse")_, and _[Kung Fu Panda 3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kung\_Fu\_Panda\_3 "Kung Fu Panda 3")_ have all grossed over $500 million) and $600 million with thirteen (_Doctor Strange_, _Moana_, and _Sing_ have all grossed over $600 million).
*   2016 was the first year since 2000 to not have films that were among the 10 highest-grossing films of all time at the time of their releases.
*   _Sing_ broke the record of a film that never reached #1 in the US with $270.3 million, passing _[My Big Fat Greek Wedding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/My\_Big\_Fat\_Greek\_Wedding "My Big Fat Greek Wedding")_ ($241.4 million in 2002–2003).

**2016 in film** is an overview of events, including the highest-grossing films, award ceremonies, festivals, a list of films released, and notable deaths.

## Evaluation of the year

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2016_in_film&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Evaluation of the year")]

In his article highlighting the best films of 2016, [Richard Brody](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Brody "Richard Brody") of _[The New Yorker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_New\_Yorker "The New Yorker")_ stated,

> Hollywood is the world's best money-laundering machine. It takes in huge amounts of money from the sale of mass-market commodities and cleanses some of it with the production of cinematic masterworks. Earning billions of dollars from C.G.I. comedies for children, superhero movies, sci-fi apocalypses, and other popular genres, the big studios channel some of those funds into movies by [Wes Anderson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wes_Anderson "Wes Anderson"), [Sofia Coppola](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sofia_Coppola "Sofia Coppola"), [Spike Lee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spike_Lee "Spike Lee"), [Martin Scorsese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martin_Scorsese "Martin Scorsese"), [James Gray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Gray_(director) "James Gray (director)"), and other worthies. Sometimes there's even an overlap between the two groups of movies, as when [Ryan Coogler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryan_Coogler "Ryan Coogler") made _[Creed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Creed\_(film) "Creed (film)")_, or when Scorsese made the modernist horror instant-classic _[Shutter Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shutter\_Island\_(film) "Shutter Island (film)")_, or when [Clint Eastwood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clint_Eastwood "Clint Eastwood") makes just about anything.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_in_film#cite_note-1)

### 2016 box office records

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2016_in_film&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: 2016 box office records")]

#### Studio records

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2016_in_film&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Studio records")]

*   [Walt Disney Studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walt_Disney_Studios_(division) "Walt Disney Studios (division)") reached $1 billion at the domestic box office faster than any other studio; it reached this goal on the 128th day of 2016, beating [Universal Studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universal_Pictures "Universal Pictures")' record of reaching the goal on the 165th day of [2015](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_in_film "2015 in film").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_in_film#cite_note-4) Disney's previous record for reaching $1 billion was on the 174th day of 2015. The studio became the first to have five of its releases (_[Rogue One](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rogue\_One "Rogue One")_, _[Finding Dory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Finding\_Dory "Finding Dory")_, _[Captain America: Civil War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Captain\_America:\_Civil\_War "Captain America: Civil War")_, _[The Jungle Book](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Jungle\_Book\_(2016\_film) "The Jungle Book (2016 film)")_, and _[Zootopia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zootopia "Zootopia")_) from a single year reach $300 million domestically. Disney also eclipsed Universal's 2015 record for most films from a single year crossing $1 billion worldwide with four (_Captain America: Civil War_, _Rogue One_, _Finding Dory_, and _Zootopia_), setting a new record for most billion-dollar-grossing films over two years with six (including _[Avengers: Age of Ultron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avengers:\_Age\_of\_Ultron "Avengers: Age of Ultron")_ and _[Star Wars: The Force Awakens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star\_Wars:\_The\_Force\_Awakens "Star Wars: The Force Awakens")_). Walt Disney Studios has also become the first studio to have the five highest-grossing films worldwide,[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_in_film#cite_note-5) and the first since at least 1913 to have the three highest-grossing films in the U.S., both in a single year. Disney became the first studio to gross more than $3 billion at the domestic box office and, with the release of _Rogue One_, became the first to gross more than $7 billion at the global box office, surpassing Universal's previous record of $6.9 billion in 2015.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_in_film#cite_note-6) Disney later passes $7 billion at the global box office again in 2018. Disney is also the first studio to have three films gross over $400 million domestically in a single year (_Rogue One_, _Finding Dory_, and _Captain America: Civil War_), and the first to fill in all slots of the top five films of any particular year.
*   Disney's [Marvel Cinematic Universe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marvel_Cinematic_Universe "Marvel Cinematic Universe") became the first film franchise to have four of its films gross over $1 billion with _Captain America: Civil War_ joining [2012](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_in_film "2012 in film")'s _[The Avengers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Avengers\_(2012\_film) "The Avengers (2012 film)")_, [2013](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_in_film "2013 in film")'s _[Iron Man 3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iron\_Man\_3 "Iron Man 3")_ and 2015's _Avengers: Age of Ultron_, and the first to gross more than $10 billion with the release of _Civil War_.

#### Film records

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2016_in_film&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Film records")]

*   _[Deadpool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deadpool\_(film) "Deadpool (film)")_ became the second-highest-grossing R-rated domestic film of all time with $363.1 million, after _[The Passion of the Christ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Passion\_of\_the\_Christ "The Passion of the Christ")_ ($370.8 million in [2004](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_in_film "2004 in film")). It later became the highest-grossing R-rated film of all time worldwide, surpassing _[The Matrix Reloaded](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Matrix\_Reloaded "The Matrix Reloaded")_, with $783.1 million. It also became the highest-grossing superhero film not to feature [Batman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Batman "Batman"), [Spider-Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spider-Man "Spider-Man"), or [Iron Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iron_Man "Iron Man") in any capacity.
*   _[Zootopia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zootopia "Zootopia")_ became the highest-grossing original animated film of all time, surpassing _[Finding Nemo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Finding\_Nemo "Finding Nemo")_ ($940.3 million in [2003](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2003_in_film "2003 in film")). Along with _[Finding Dory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Finding\_Dory "Finding Dory")_, it became one of two animated films to earn over $1 billion in the same year, a first.
*   _[Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Batman\_v\_Superman:\_Dawn\_of\_Justice "Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice")_ had the biggest worldwide opening weekend ever for a superhero film with $422.5 million, surpassing _The Avengers_ ($392.5 million in 2012). The film, along with _Captain America: Civil War_, were the most expensive films of the year ($250 million).
*   _[Dangal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dangal\_(2016\_film) "Dangal (2016 film)")_ became the highest-grossing [Indian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cinema_of_India "Cinema of India") film of all-time, partly due to successful ticket-sales in [China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China "China").
*   _[The Mermaid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Mermaid\_(2016\_film) "The Mermaid (2016 film)")_ became the [highest-grossing film ever in China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_highest-grossing_films_in_China "List of highest-grossing films in China") and the first film ever to earn over $500 million without a wide North American release.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_in_film#cite_note-7)
*   _[Shin Godzilla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shin\_Godzilla "Shin Godzilla")_, the 31st Godzilla film, grossed about ¥82.5 billion ($77.9 million), making it the highest-grossing Japanese-made film in the franchise, the most successful live-action Japanese film in 2016, and the second-most successful film of the year in Japan.
*   The [anime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anime "Anime") film _[Your Name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Your\_Name "Your Name")_ grossed US$354 million,[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_in_film#cite_note-8) becoming the [highest-grossing anime film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_highest-grossing_anime_films "List of highest-grossing anime films"), the [fourth-highest-grossing film in Japan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_highest-grossing_films_in_Japan "List of highest-grossing films in Japan"), and the [seventh-highest-grossing traditionally animated film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_highest-grossing_animated_films#Traditional_animation "List of highest-grossing animated films"). In [China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China "China"), it grossed US$81.3 million, becoming the highest-grossing 2D animated film[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_in_film#cite_note-9) and the highest-grossing Japanese film in the world's second-largest movie market,[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_in_film#cite_note-10) as well as the highest-grossing non-Hollywood foreign film in China until it was surpassed by Indian film _[Dangal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dangal\_(2016\_film) "Dangal (2016 film)")_.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_in_film#cite_note-usnews-11)
*   _[Warcraft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warcraft\_(film) "Warcraft (film)")_ became the highest-grossing [video game adaptation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_films_based_on_video_games "List of films based on video games") worldwide, with $433.5 million,[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_in_film#cite_note-12) surpassing _[Prince of Persia: The Sands of Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prince\_of\_Persia:\_The\_Sands\_of\_Time\_(film) "Prince of Persia: The Sands of Time (film)")_ ($336.4 million in [2010](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_in_film "2010 in film")).
*   _Finding Dory_ grossed $135.1 million domestically and $185.7 million worldwide in its opening weekend, setting records for the biggest domestic opening weekend for both Pixar (surpassing _[Toy Story 3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toy\_Story\_3 "Toy Story 3")_, with $110.3 million in 2010) and any animated film (surpassing _[Shrek the Third](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shrek\_the\_Third "Shrek the Third")_, with $121.6 million in [2007](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_in_film "2007 in film")), the biggest worldwide opening weekend for Pixar (surpassing _[Inside Out](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inside\_Out "Inside Out")_, with $180.1 million in 2015), and the second-biggest opening weekend worldwide for an animated film after _[Ice Age: Dawn of the Dinosaurs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ice\_Age:\_Dawn\_of\_the\_Dinosaurs "Ice Age: Dawn of the Dinosaurs")_ ($218.4 million in [2009](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_in_film "2009 in film")). It later became the highest-grossing animated film at the domestic box office, surpassing _[Shrek 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shrek\_2 "Shrek 2")_ ($441.2 million in 2004). It became the first animated film to cross $450, $460, $470, and $480 million at the domestic box office. Along with _Zootopia_, it became one of two animated films to earn over $1 billion in the same year, a first. It also became the eighth film to do so during the two-year period of 2015–16, surpassing the previous record of seven billion-dollar films during the two-year period of 2011–12.
*   _[The Secret Life of Pets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Secret\_Life\_of\_Pets "The Secret Life of Pets")_ grossed $104.4 million domestically in its opening weekend, breaking _Inside Out_'s record ($90.4 million) for the highest domestic opening weekend for an original film of any kind, and became the first original film to open above $100 million domestically. It also became the highest-grossing original non-Disney animated film ever, both domestically (surpassing _[Despicable Me](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Despicable\_Me "Despicable Me")_, with $251.5 million in 2010) and worldwide (beating _[Kung Fu Panda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kung\_Fu\_Panda\_(film) "Kung Fu Panda (film)")_, with $631.7 million in [2008](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_in_film "2008 in film")).
*   _[Sausage Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sausage\_Party "Sausage Party")_ became the highest-grossing R-rated animated film of all time ($140.7 million), surpassing _[South Park: Bigger, Longer & Uncut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South\_Park:\_Bigger,\_Longer\_&\_Uncut "South Park: Bigger, Longer & Uncut")_ ($83.1 million in 1999).
*   _[Doctor Strange](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor\_Strange\_(2016\_film) "Doctor Strange (2016 film)")_ became the highest-grossing single-character debut of any Marvel Cinematic Universe film worldwide with $677.7 million, beating _[Iron Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iron\_Man\_(2008\_film) "Iron Man (2008 film)")_ ($585.2 million in 2008).
*   2016 became the first year to have ten films to cross $700 million worldwide, beating 2014's record of nine films. It also surpassed the latter year in terms of most films earning more than $500 million with sixteen (_Doctor Strange_, _[Moana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana\_(2016\_film) "Moana (2016 film)")_, _[Sing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sing\_(2016\_American\_film) "Sing (2016 American film)")_, _The Mermaid_, _[X-Men: Apocalypse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/X-Men:\_Apocalypse "X-Men: Apocalypse")_, and _[Kung Fu Panda 3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kung\_Fu\_Panda\_3 "Kung Fu Panda 3")_ have all grossed over $500 million) and $600 million with thirteen (_Doctor Strange_, _Moana_, and _Sing_ have all grossed over $600 million).
*   2016 was the first year since 2000 to not have films that were among the 10 highest-grossing films of all time at the time of their releases.
*   _Sing_ broke the record of a film that never reached #1 in the US with $270.3 million, passing _[My Big Fat Greek Wedding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/My\_Big\_Fat\_Greek\_Wedding "My Big Fat Greek Wedding")_ ($241.4 million in 2002–2003).

**The Band Camino** (stylized as **The Band CAMINO**) is an American [rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_music "Rock music") band. Established in [Memphis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Memphis,_Tennessee "Memphis, Tennessee"), [Tennessee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tennessee "Tennessee"), in 2015, the group is now based in [Nashville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nashville "Nashville").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Band_Camino#cite_note-atwoodmagazine-1)

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Band_Camino&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

Andrew Isbell, Jeffery Jordan, Graham Rowell, and Spencer Stewart established the Band Camino in 2015 while the four were students at the [University of Memphis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Memphis "University of Memphis"). Isbell played drums, Rowell was bassist, and Jordan and Stewart sang and played guitar.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Band_Camino#cite_note-amgbio-2) The band released their first EP in 2016, _My Thoughts On You_.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Band_Camino#cite_note-substream3-3) Their second EP, _Heaven_, was released in 2017;[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Band_Camino#cite_note-substream1-4) Isbell left the band around this time and was replaced by Garrison Burgess.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Band_Camino#cite_note-amgbio-2)

By May 2019, the Band Camino had signed to [Elektra Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elektra_Records "Elektra Records") and released an EP _tryhard_, in August.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Band_Camino#cite_note-substream1-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Band_Camino#cite_note-substream2-5) To promote the release, the group embarked on a headlining tour of North America from September through October, plus two dates in the United Kingdom.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Band_Camino#cite_note-substream1-4) On April 9, 2020, bassist Graham Rowell was removed from the group after accusations of sexual misconduct between him and fans surfaced online.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Band_Camino#cite_note-6) Later that year on July 31, 2020, the band released "Crying Over You" with [Chelsea Cutler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_Cutler "Chelsea Cutler").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Band_Camino#cite_note-7)

On December 11, 2020, the group released its first song, "Roses", from its self-titled album.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Band_Camino#cite_note-substream1-4) This was followed by "1 Last Cigarette" on February 26, 2021, "Sorry Mom" on April 30,[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Band_Camino#cite_note-peoplemagazine1-8) and "Know It All" on June 25.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Band_Camino#cite_note-RS-KIA-9) Their self-titled debut album was released on September 10, 2021.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Band_Camino#cite_note-RS-KIA-9)

On February 21, 2023, the band released their first single since 2021, "Told You So", and went on tour in Europe.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Band_Camino#cite_note-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Band_Camino#cite_note-11) On April 21, 2023, the band released their next single, "What Am I Missing?".[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Band_Camino#cite_note-12) On May 26, 2023 the band released their third track from the album, "Last Man in the World".[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Band_Camino#cite_note-13) On June 17, 2023, the band performed at the [Bonnaroo Music & Arts Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bonnaroo_Music_Festival "Bonnaroo Music Festival") for the first time.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Band_Camino#cite_note-14) On June 26, 2023, the band then announced their second album, _The Dark_ which was released on August 11, 2023, alongside a North American headlining tour titled "Screaming In The Dark Tour" and released a single titled "See You Later".[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Band_Camino#cite_note-15) On February 25, 2024, the band performed in Manila, Philippines for the first time as part of the Bobapalooza Music and Arts Festival.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Band_Camino#cite_note-16)

On May 13, 2024, the band announced its next EP, _Bruises_, which was released on May 17, 2024, alongside a summer tour titled "The Taking Shape Tour".[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Band_Camino#cite_note-17)

On July 25, 2025 the band released its next album, _NeverAlways_ (later retitled to _NeverAlways (Vol. 1)_), featuring the singles "Baggy Jeans", "Stupid Questions", and "What You Can't Have". A single later found on _NeverAlways (Vol. 2)_, "12:34" was released three months later on October 6, 2025 at 12:34 PM CT. The second single, "Afterthought" was released on December 3, 2025, 3.5 years since its first tease on TikTok, which garnered attention among their fanbase, leading the band to finally release it.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Band_Camino#cite_note-18) Their third single, "Holly!", was released on April 17, 2026 alongside an announcement of _NeverAlways (Vol. 2)_, the second half of the double album which was released on May 26, 2026 and was preceded by a fourth single, "Do What You Gotta Do" two days earlier.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Band_Camino#cite_note-19)

## Musical style
