**The Band Camino** (stylized as **The Band CAMINO**) is an American [rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_music "Rock music") band. Established in [Memphis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Memphis,_Tennessee "Memphis, Tennessee"), [Tennessee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tennessee "Tennessee"), in 2015, the group is now based in [Nashville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nashville "Nashville").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Band_Camino#cite_note-atwoodmagazine-1)

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Band_Camino&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

Andrew Isbell, Jeffery Jordan, Graham Rowell, and Spencer Stewart established the Band Camino in 2015 while the four were students at the [University of Memphis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Memphis "University of Memphis"). Isbell played drums, Rowell was bassist, and Jordan and Stewart sang and played guitar.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Band_Camino#cite_note-amgbio-2) The band released their first EP in 2016, _My Thoughts On You_.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Band_Camino#cite_note-substream3-3) Their second EP, _Heaven_, was released in 2017;[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Band_Camino#cite_note-substream1-4) Isbell left the band around this time and was replaced by Garrison Burgess.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Band_Camino#cite_note-amgbio-2)

By May 2019, the Band Camino had signed to [Elektra Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elektra_Records "Elektra Records") and released an EP _tryhard_, in August.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Band_Camino#cite_note-substream1-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Band_Camino#cite_note-substream2-5) To promote the release, the group embarked on a headlining tour of North America from September through October, plus two dates in the United Kingdom.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Band_Camino#cite_note-substream1-4) On April 9, 2020, bassist Graham Rowell was removed from the group after accusations of sexual misconduct between him and fans surfaced online.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Band_Camino#cite_note-6) Later that year on July 31, 2020, the band released "Crying Over You" with [Chelsea Cutler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_Cutler "Chelsea Cutler").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Band_Camino#cite_note-7)

On December 11, 2020, the group released its first song, "Roses", from its self-titled album.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Band_Camino#cite_note-substream1-4) This was followed by "1 Last Cigarette" on February 26, 2021, "Sorry Mom" on April 30,[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Band_Camino#cite_note-peoplemagazine1-8) and "Know It All" on June 25.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Band_Camino#cite_note-RS-KIA-9) Their self-titled debut album was released on September 10, 2021.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Band_Camino#cite_note-RS-KIA-9)

On February 21, 2023, the band released their first single since 2021, "Told You So", and went on tour in Europe.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Band_Camino#cite_note-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Band_Camino#cite_note-11) On April 21, 2023, the band released their next single, "What Am I Missing?".[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Band_Camino#cite_note-12) On May 26, 2023 the band released their third track from the album, "Last Man in the World".[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Band_Camino#cite_note-13) On June 17, 2023, the band performed at the [Bonnaroo Music & Arts Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bonnaroo_Music_Festival "Bonnaroo Music Festival") for the first time.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Band_Camino#cite_note-14) On June 26, 2023, the band then announced their second album, _The Dark_ which was released on August 11, 2023, alongside a North American headlining tour titled "Screaming In The Dark Tour" and released a single titled "See You Later".[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Band_Camino#cite_note-15) On February 25, 2024, the band performed in Manila, Philippines for the first time as part of the Bobapalooza Music and Arts Festival.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Band_Camino#cite_note-16)

On May 13, 2024, the band announced its next EP, _Bruises_, which was released on May 17, 2024, alongside a summer tour titled "The Taking Shape Tour".[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Band_Camino#cite_note-17)

On July 25, 2025 the band released its next album, _NeverAlways_ (later retitled to _NeverAlways (Vol. 1)_), featuring the singles "Baggy Jeans", "Stupid Questions", and "What You Can't Have". A single later found on _NeverAlways (Vol. 2)_, "12:34" was released three months later on October 6, 2025 at 12:34 PM CT. The second single, "Afterthought" was released on December 3, 2025, 3.5 years since its first tease on TikTok, which garnered attention among their fanbase, leading the band to finally release it.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Band_Camino#cite_note-18) Their third single, "Holly!", was released on April 17, 2026 alongside an announcement of _NeverAlways (Vol. 2)_, the second half of the double album which was released on May 26, 2026 and was preceded by a fourth single, "Do What You Gotta Do" two days earlier.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Band_Camino#cite_note-19)

## Musical style

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Band_Camino&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Musical style")]

Timothy Monger at [Allmusic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allmusic "Allmusic") describes the Band Camino's musical approach as a blend of [indie rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indie_rock "Indie rock") and [electropop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electropop "Electropop").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Band_Camino#cite_note-amgbio-2)

**The Aces** (formerly **The Blue Aces**) are an American [alternative pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alternative_pop "Alternative pop") band from [Provo, Utah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Provo,_Utah "Provo, Utah").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Aces_(indie_pop_band)#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Aces_(indie_pop_band)#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Aces_(indie_pop_band)#cite_note-3) The band has four members: guitarist Katie Henderson, bassist McKenna Petty, and sisters Alisa Ramirez (drums) and Cristal Ramirez (lead vocals and guitars).[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Aces_(indie_pop_band)#cite_note-4)

Their first single as the Aces, "Stuck", was released in 2016, eventually reaching #38 on the _[Billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard\_(magazine) "Billboard (magazine)")_[Alternative Songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alternative_Airplay "Alternative Airplay") chart in late 2017.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Aces_(indie_pop_band)#cite_note-:0-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Aces_(indie_pop_band)#cite_note-6) The band's second single, "Physical", was released in 2017 in advance of their debut EP, _I Don't Like Being Honest_.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Aces_(indie_pop_band)#cite_note-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Aces_(indie_pop_band)#cite_note-8) The band was signed to [Red Bull Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Bull_Records "Red Bull Records"). The band's debut album, _[When My Heart Felt Volcanic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/When\_My\_Heart\_Felt\_Volcanic "When My Heart Felt Volcanic")_, was released on April 6, 2018.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Aces_(indie_pop_band)#cite_note-9) The Aces worked with six producers on the records, but Dan Gibson and Simon Oscroft were particularly influential, being involved in half of the material.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Aces_(indie_pop_band)#cite_note-10)

The Aces joined [5 Seconds of Summer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/5_Seconds_of_Summer "5 Seconds of Summer") for their [Meet You There Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meet_You_There_Tour "Meet You There Tour"). Following this tour, they embarked on their own North American headlining tour in support of _When My Heart Felt Volcanic_, the Waiting For You Tour.

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Aces_(indie_pop_band)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Career")]

### Origin

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Aces_(indie_pop_band)&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Origin")]

The Aces began when sisters Cristal and Alisa Ramirez were ten and eight years old respectively. Although neither sister recalls exactly when their musical career visions began, the Ramirez sisters were raised in a music-loving household where their father would dance salsa with them and their mother played 1980s pop artists like Whitney Houston and Michael Jackson, as well as older brother playing in many prominent Provo/SLC hardcore punk bands.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Aces_(indie_pop_band)#cite_note-11) With a piqued interest, they began to jam out while studying and taking notes from their favorite bands on YouTube.

One Christmas season, the sisters asked their best friend, McKenna Petty, to ask for a bass for Christmas. Soon after, the trio, all self-taught, formed the Blue Aces. They began to jam and experiment in their neighbor's garage. In 2008 the band was officially formed when Petty's friend, Katie Henderson, joined the group.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Aces_(indie_pop_band)#cite_note-12) Collectively, the Aces began to sharpen their talents and get their raw exposure throughout high school while performing locally at venues and bars. Over the years, as they expanded their presence within their local music scene they were listed on the “Top 10 Best Bands in Provo” by Provo Buzz and “10 Best Utah Bands You Should Know” by Paste Magazine.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Aces_(indie_pop_band)#cite_note-13) In 2014, the girls decided to professionally pursue a musical career after watching 18-year-old [Lorde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lorde "Lorde") win her first Grammy.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Aces_(indie_pop_band)#cite_note-14)

With no industry ties, the girls began their hunt for professional connections first starting by working with accomplished producers. Particularly the key to buzz surrounding them, record labels soon came calling for them. In 2016, Red Bull Records signed them. The band was signed by A&R executive Kenny "Tick" Salcido.

### As the Blue Aces (2012–2014)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Aces_(indie_pop_band)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: As the Blue Aces (2012–2014)")]

Katie Henderson, McKenna Petty, Alisa Ramirez, and Cristal Ramirez started as the Blue Aces in 2012. They released two EPs as the Blue Aces before they changed their name to the Aces.

### _I Don't Like Being Honest_ (2014–2017)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Aces_(indie_pop_band)&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: I Don't Like Being Honest (2014–2017)")]

In 2016, they wrote two songs independently: "Volcanic Love" and "Stuck". Soon after, the Aces were signed with Red Bull Records and the band embarked on songwriting and recording sessions.

On June 23, 2017, the band's debut EP (under the new name), _I Don't Like Being Honest_, was released. Their debut single, "Stuck", reached No. 38 on the _Billboard_ Alternative Songs chart.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Aces_(indie_pop_band)#cite_note-:0-5) During SXSW they performed at Nylon, Noisey, Rachael Ray's Feedback House, and Quantum Collective's SX Invasion. For the rest of 2017, the Aces found themselves sharing the stage with alternative bands such as [Joywave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joywave "Joywave") and [Portugal. The Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portugal._The_Man "Portugal. The Man").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Aces_(indie_pop_band)#cite_note-15)

### _When My Heart Felt Volcanic_ (2018–2019)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Aces_(indie_pop_band)&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: When My Heart Felt Volcanic (2018–2019)")]

[![Image 5: The band onstage](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/fb/The_Aces_05_25_2018_-40_%2842366996605%29.jpg/250px-The_Aces_05_25_2018_-40_%2842366996605%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:The_Aces_05_25_2018_-40_(42366996605).jpg)

The Aces in 2018

Early February 2018, the Aces teased their upcoming debut album. To celebrate, they announced their tour with indie pop band, [Coin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coin_(band) "Coin (band)"). Two months later, on April 6, 2018, the Aces released _[When My Heart Felt Volcanic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/When\_My\_Heart\_Felt\_Volcanic "When My Heart Felt Volcanic")_. On May 16, 2018, The band performed on Seth Meyer's _Late Night Show._ Their song “Strong Enough” was featured on the soundtrack of _[NBA 2K20](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA\_2K20 "NBA 2K20")_.

The Aces were announced as the opening act for [5 Seconds of Summer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/5_Seconds_of_Summer "5 Seconds of Summer")'s [Meet You There World Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meet_You_There_Tour "Meet You There Tour"). Subsequently, they announced their first ever headlining tours in the US and Europe, _When My Heart Felt Volcanic_, the Waiting For You Tour. They played festival stages and larger venues for the rest of 2018 and early 2019.

### _Under My Influence_ (2020–2022)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Aces_(indie_pop_band)&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Under My Influence (2020–2022)")]

On March 4, 2020, the Aces released their first single of their second LP, titled "Daydream". A music video for the song was released on March 24, 2020.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Aces_(indie_pop_band)#cite_note-16)

On April 6, 2020, the second single was released, titled "Lost Angeles". On May 6, 2020, the Aces revealed the title and track listing of the album, _[Under My Influence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Under\_My\_Influence "Under My Influence")_, along with the release of a third single, "My Phone is Trying to Kill Me".

Their fourth single from _Under My Influence_, "Kelly" was released on June 1, 2020. "Kelly," which is explicitly queer, is the first of the band's songs to use gendered pronouns. Cristal and Alisa Ramirez commented that while they had not been consciously avoiding gendered pronouns, the band, in which three of four members are queer, had previously not been ready to "step into that space [...] as artists."[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Aces_(indie_pop_band)#cite_note-17)

_Under My Influence_ was originally slated for release on June 12, 2020.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Aces_(indie_pop_band)#cite_note-18)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Aces_(indie_pop_band)#cite_note-19) However, on June 7, the band announced that the album would be delayed in response to the [George Floyd protests](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Floyd_protests "George Floyd protests").[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Aces_(indie_pop_band)#cite_note-20) The band's official website revealed the new release date as July 17, 2020.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Aces_(indie_pop_band)#cite_note-The_Aces_Official-21)

### _I've Loved You for So Long_ (2023–2024)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Aces_(indie_pop_band)&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: I've Loved You for So Long (2023–2024)")]

On June 8, 2022, The Aces released the first single from their third LP, titled "Girls Make Me Wanna Die". The official music video was released on June 29, 2022[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Aces_(indie_pop_band)#cite_note-22)

On February 17, 2023, the second single was released, titled "Always Get This Way". The Album, [_I've Loved You For So Long_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I've_Loved_You_for_So_Long "I've Loved You for So Long"), was officially announced on February 21, 2023.

On March 31, 2023, The third single was released, titled "Solo". The 4th single and title track, "I've Loved You For So Long" was released on April 28, 2023.

On June 2, 2023, the Aces released their third LP, titled _[I've Loved You for So Long](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I've\_Loved\_You\_for\_So\_Long "I've Loved You for So Long")_.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Aces_(indie_pop_band)#cite_note-23)

### _Gold Star Baby_ (2025-present)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Aces_(indie_pop_band)&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Gold Star Baby (2025-present)")]

On August 15, 2025, the Aces released their fourth studio album _[Gold Star Baby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gold\_Star\_Baby "Gold Star Baby")_.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Aces_(indie_pop_band)#cite_note-24)

## Band members

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Aces_(indie_pop_band)&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Band members")]

The Aces consists of Katie Henderson, McKenna Petty, Alisa Ramirez, and Cristal Ramirez. The band started while they were all in school together. Sisters Cristal and Alisa Ramirez, along with their best friends, decided to turn their musical after school get-togethers into a career.

*   Cristal Ramirez – lead vocals and guitar
*   Katie Henderson – guitar and vocals
*   McKenna Petty – bass and vocals
*   Alisa Ramirez – drums and vocals

## Musical style

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Aces_(indie_pop_band)&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Musical style")]

The Aces have cited as musical and career influences [Paramore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paramore "Paramore"); [Earth, Wind & Fire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earth,_Wind_&_Fire "Earth, Wind & Fire"); [The Beatles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Beatles "The Beatles"); [New Order](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Order_(band) "New Order (band)"); [Depeche Mode](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Depeche_Mode "Depeche Mode"); [Michael Jackson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Jackson "Michael Jackson"); and [Weezer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weezer "Weezer").[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Aces_(indie_pop_band)#cite_note-25) Their musical style has been described as [indie pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indie_pop "Indie pop") and [alternative pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alternative_pop "Alternative pop").

## Gender as a media focus

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Aces_(indie_pop_band)&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Gender as a media focus")]

The Aces are an all-female band and members have expressed the desire to break the idea of the "girl band/girl group" genre. The media has often looked at gender first rather than their music when referring to the Aces, according to Cristal Ramirez, who said in an interview with Capitol Sound DC, "we _are_ just a band! I don’t see why people have to see gender all the time and make it a thing. But at the same time, it is unique and it is a strength of ours that we are all women. We wanna inspire other girls and we get that all the time–fans coming up to us and being like ‘oh my gosh you guys are so inspiring I wanna be in the music industry’ or ‘I wanna start a band.'"[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Aces_(indie_pop_band)#cite_note-26)

**The Aces** (formerly **The Blue Aces**) are an American [alternative pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alternative_pop "Alternative pop") band from [Provo, Utah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Provo,_Utah "Provo, Utah").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Aces_(indie_pop_band)#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Aces_(indie_pop_band)#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Aces_(indie_pop_band)#cite_note-3) The band has four members: guitarist Katie Henderson, bassist McKenna Petty, and sisters Alisa Ramirez (drums) and Cristal Ramirez (lead vocals and guitars).[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Aces_(indie_pop_band)#cite_note-4)

Their first single as the Aces, "Stuck", was released in 2016, eventually reaching #38 on the _[Billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard\_(magazine) "Billboard (magazine)")_[Alternative Songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alternative_Airplay "Alternative Airplay") chart in late 2017.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Aces_(indie_pop_band)#cite_note-:0-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Aces_(indie_pop_band)#cite_note-6) The band's second single, "Physical", was released in 2017 in advance of their debut EP, _I Don't Like Being Honest_.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Aces_(indie_pop_band)#cite_note-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Aces_(indie_pop_band)#cite_note-8) The band was signed to [Red Bull Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Bull_Records "Red Bull Records"). The band's debut album, _[When My Heart Felt Volcanic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/When\_My\_Heart\_Felt\_Volcanic "When My Heart Felt Volcanic")_, was released on April 6, 2018.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Aces_(indie_pop_band)#cite_note-9) The Aces worked with six producers on the records, but Dan Gibson and Simon Oscroft were particularly influential, being involved in half of the material.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Aces_(indie_pop_band)#cite_note-10)

The Aces joined [5 Seconds of Summer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/5_Seconds_of_Summer "5 Seconds of Summer") for their [Meet You There Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meet_You_There_Tour "Meet You There Tour"). Following this tour, they embarked on their own North American headlining tour in support of _When My Heart Felt Volcanic_, the Waiting For You Tour.

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Aces_(indie_pop_band)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Career")]

### Origin

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Aces_(indie_pop_band)&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Origin")]

The Aces began when sisters Cristal and Alisa Ramirez were ten and eight years old respectively. Although neither sister recalls exactly when their musical career visions began, the Ramirez sisters were raised in a music-loving household where their father would dance salsa with them and their mother played 1980s pop artists like Whitney Houston and Michael Jackson, as well as older brother playing in many prominent Provo/SLC hardcore punk bands.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Aces_(indie_pop_band)#cite_note-11) With a piqued interest, they began to jam out while studying and taking notes from their favorite bands on YouTube.

One Christmas season, the sisters asked their best friend, McKenna Petty, to ask for a bass for Christmas. Soon after, the trio, all self-taught, formed the Blue Aces. They began to jam and experiment in their neighbor's garage. In 2008 the band was officially formed when Petty's friend, Katie Henderson, joined the group.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Aces_(indie_pop_band)#cite_note-12) Collectively, the Aces began to sharpen their talents and get their raw exposure throughout high school while performing locally at venues and bars. Over the years, as they expanded their presence within their local music scene they were listed on the “Top 10 Best Bands in Provo” by Provo Buzz and “10 Best Utah Bands You Should Know” by Paste Magazine.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Aces_(indie_pop_band)#cite_note-13) In 2014, the girls decided to professionally pursue a musical career after watching 18-year-old [Lorde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lorde "Lorde") win her first Grammy.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Aces_(indie_pop_band)#cite_note-14)

With no industry ties, the girls began their hunt for professional connections first starting by working with accomplished producers. Particularly the key to buzz surrounding them, record labels soon came calling for them. In 2016, Red Bull Records signed them. The band was signed by A&R executive Kenny "Tick" Salcido.

### As the Blue Aces (2012–2014)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Aces_(indie_pop_band)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: As the Blue Aces (2012–2014)")]

Katie Henderson, McKenna Petty, Alisa Ramirez, and Cristal Ramirez started as the Blue Aces in 2012. They released two EPs as the Blue Aces before they changed their name to the Aces.

### _I Don't Like Being Honest_ (2014–2017)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Aces_(indie_pop_band)&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: I Don't Like Being Honest (2014–2017)")]

In 2016, they wrote two songs independently: "Volcanic Love" and "Stuck". Soon after, the Aces were signed with Red Bull Records and the band embarked on songwriting and recording sessions.

On June 23, 2017, the band's debut EP (under the new name), _I Don't Like Being Honest_, was released. Their debut single, "Stuck", reached No. 38 on the _Billboard_ Alternative Songs chart.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Aces_(indie_pop_band)#cite_note-:0-5) During SXSW they performed at Nylon, Noisey, Rachael Ray's Feedback House, and Quantum Collective's SX Invasion. For the rest of 2017, the Aces found themselves sharing the stage with alternative bands such as [Joywave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joywave "Joywave") and [Portugal. The Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portugal._The_Man "Portugal. The Man").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Aces_(indie_pop_band)#cite_note-15)

### _When My Heart Felt Volcanic_ (2018–2019)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Aces_(indie_pop_band)&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: When My Heart Felt Volcanic (2018–2019)")]

[![Image 5: The band onstage](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/fb/The_Aces_05_25_2018_-40_%2842366996605%29.jpg/250px-The_Aces_05_25_2018_-40_%2842366996605%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:The_Aces_05_25_2018_-40_(42366996605).jpg)

The Aces in 2018

Early February 2018, the Aces teased their upcoming debut album. To celebrate, they announced their tour with indie pop band, [Coin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coin_(band) "Coin (band)"). Two months later, on April 6, 2018, the Aces released _[When My Heart Felt Volcanic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/When\_My\_Heart\_Felt\_Volcanic "When My Heart Felt Volcanic")_. On May 16, 2018, The band performed on Seth Meyer's _Late Night Show._ Their song “Strong Enough” was featured on the soundtrack of _[NBA 2K20](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA\_2K20 "NBA 2K20")_.

The Aces were announced as the opening act for [5 Seconds of Summer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/5_Seconds_of_Summer "5 Seconds of Summer")'s [Meet You There World Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meet_You_There_Tour "Meet You There Tour"). Subsequently, they announced their first ever headlining tours in the US and Europe, _When My Heart Felt Volcanic_, the Waiting For You Tour. They played festival stages and larger venues for the rest of 2018 and early 2019.

### _Under My Influence_ (2020–2022)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Aces_(indie_pop_band)&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Under My Influence (2020–2022)")]

On March 4, 2020, the Aces released their first single of their second LP, titled "Daydream". A music video for the song was released on March 24, 2020.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Aces_(indie_pop_band)#cite_note-16)

On April 6, 2020, the second single was released, titled "Lost Angeles". On May 6, 2020, the Aces revealed the title and track listing of the album, _[Under My Influence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Under\_My\_Influence "Under My Influence")_, along with the release of a third single, "My Phone is Trying to Kill Me".

Their fourth single from _Under My Influence_, "Kelly" was released on June 1, 2020. "Kelly," which is explicitly queer, is the first of the band's songs to use gendered pronouns. Cristal and Alisa Ramirez commented that while they had not been consciously avoiding gendered pronouns, the band, in which three of four members are queer, had previously not been ready to "step into that space [...] as artists."[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Aces_(indie_pop_band)#cite_note-17)

_Under My Influence_ was originally slated for release on June 12, 2020.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Aces_(indie_pop_band)#cite_note-18)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Aces_(indie_pop_band)#cite_note-19) However, on June 7, the band announced that the album would be delayed in response to the [George Floyd protests](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Floyd_protests "George Floyd protests").[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Aces_(indie_pop_band)#cite_note-20) The band's official website revealed the new release date as July 17, 2020.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Aces_(indie_pop_band)#cite_note-The_Aces_Official-21)

### _I've Loved You for So Long_ (2023–2024)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Aces_(indie_pop_band)&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: I've Loved You for So Long (2023–2024)")]

On June 8, 2022, The Aces released the first single from their third LP, titled "Girls Make Me Wanna Die". The official music video was released on June 29, 2022[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Aces_(indie_pop_band)#cite_note-22)

On February 17, 2023, the second single was released, titled "Always Get This Way". The Album, [_I've Loved You For So Long_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I've_Loved_You_for_So_Long "I've Loved You for So Long"), was officially announced on February 21, 2023.

On March 31, 2023, The third single was released, titled "Solo". The 4th single and title track, "I've Loved You For So Long" was released on April 28, 2023.

On June 2, 2023, the Aces released their third LP, titled _[I've Loved You for So Long](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I've\_Loved\_You\_for\_So\_Long "I've Loved You for So Long")_.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Aces_(indie_pop_band)#cite_note-23)

### _Gold Star Baby_ (2025-present)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Aces_(indie_pop_band)&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Gold Star Baby (2025-present)")]

On August 15, 2025, the Aces released their fourth studio album _[Gold Star Baby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gold\_Star\_Baby "Gold Star Baby")_.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Aces_(indie_pop_band)#cite_note-24)

## Band members

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Aces_(indie_pop_band)&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Band members")]

The Aces consists of Katie Henderson, McKenna Petty, Alisa Ramirez, and Cristal Ramirez. The band started while they were all in school together. Sisters Cristal and Alisa Ramirez, along with their best friends, decided to turn their musical after school get-togethers into a career.

*   Cristal Ramirez – lead vocals and guitar
*   Katie Henderson – guitar and vocals
*   McKenna Petty – bass and vocals
*   Alisa Ramirez – drums and vocals

## Musical style

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Aces_(indie_pop_band)&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Musical style")]

The Aces have cited as musical and career influences [Paramore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paramore "Paramore"); [Earth, Wind & Fire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earth,_Wind_&_Fire "Earth, Wind & Fire"); [The Beatles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Beatles "The Beatles"); [New Order](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Order_(band) "New Order (band)"); [Depeche Mode](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Depeche_Mode "Depeche Mode"); [Michael Jackson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Jackson "Michael Jackson"); and [Weezer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weezer "Weezer").[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Aces_(indie_pop_band)#cite_note-25) Their musical style has been described as [indie pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indie_pop "Indie pop") and [alternative pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alternative_pop "Alternative pop").

## Gender as a media focus

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Aces_(indie_pop_band)&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Gender as a media focus")]

The Aces are an all-female band and members have expressed the desire to break the idea of the "girl band/girl group" genre. The media has often looked at gender first rather than their music when referring to the Aces, according to Cristal Ramirez, who said in an interview with Capitol Sound DC, "we _are_ just a band! I don’t see why people have to see gender all the time and make it a thing. But at the same time, it is unique and it is a strength of ours that we are all women. We wanna inspire other girls and we get that all the time–fans coming up to us and being like ‘oh my gosh you guys are so inspiring I wanna be in the music industry’ or ‘I wanna start a band.'"[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Aces_(indie_pop_band)#cite_note-26)

_**A Quiet Place (Music from the Motion Picture)**_ is the [soundtrack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soundtrack "Soundtrack") to the [2018 film of the same name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Quiet_Place "A Quiet Place") directed by [John Krasinski](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Krasinski "John Krasinski"). Featuring musical score composed by [Marco Beltrami](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marco_Beltrami "Marco Beltrami"), the soundtrack was released under the [Milan Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milan_Records "Milan Records") label on April 6, 2018.

## Development

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=A_Quiet_Place_(soundtrack)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Development")]

Marco Beltrami had composed the musical score for _A Quiet Place_.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Quiet_Place_(soundtrack)#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Quiet_Place_(soundtrack)#cite_note-2) He signed the film over the occasion of [Thanksgiving](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thanksgiving_(United_States) "Thanksgiving (United States)") (November 23, 2017) and was set to compose the score by early-January 2018 in a short span of time while Beltrami was also scoring the [National Geographic Films](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Geographic_Films "National Geographic Films") documentary _[Free Solo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free\_Solo "Free Solo")_.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Quiet_Place_(soundtrack)#cite_note-:0-3) Due to the film's limited budget, Beltrami refrained from using a full-fledged orchestra for recording as "the film is truly intimate and contained". He used a small ensemble of 30 musicians which involved strings and piano and extensively manipulated and processed the score "so that we could create sounds that were semi-orchestral and semi-electronic".[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Quiet_Place_(soundtrack)#cite_note-4)

The initial blueprint for the original score came from Krasinski's passion for the cover version of [David Bowie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Bowie "David Bowie")'s "[Heroes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%22Heroes%22_(David_Bowie_song) "\"Heroes\" (David Bowie song)")" by [Peter Gabriel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel "Peter Gabriel"). Krasinski played the song to Beltrami while scoring the film and it became the basis of the score to Beltrami. He composed a family theme and sent to Krasinski which he liked it and eventually included into the edit. For the sound-hunting creatures, he wanted to come up with "a signature monster sound, something we haven't heard before that instills fear, even if the monster isn't onscreen".[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Quiet_Place_(soundtrack)#cite_note-:0-3) This resulted in the opening theme "It Hears You". Beltrami felt recording the final cue was difficult to him, as "when they realize that they can kill the monsters and the monsters are racing toward them, that cue was really crucial to the process [...] Once I solved that, everything else fell into place. It's not a melodic cue, but it's a driving force which led to the monster cue."[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Quiet_Place_(soundtrack)#cite_note-:0-3)

Most of the score had been excluded from the film, which Krasinski found impactful having the score dominated the scenes.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Quiet_Place_(soundtrack)#cite_note-IGN_18-5) Beltrami provided supervising sound editors [Erik Aadahl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erik_Aadahl "Erik Aadahl") and [Ethan Van der Ryn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethan_Van_der_Ryn "Ethan Van der Ryn") music to work in a way that would not interfere with the sound design throughout the film.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Quiet_Place_(soundtrack)#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Quiet_Place_(soundtrack)#cite_note-7)

## Release

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=A_Quiet_Place_(soundtrack)&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Release")]

The soundtrack to _A Quiet Place_ was released under the [Milan Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milan_Records "Milan Records") label on April 6, 2018.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Quiet_Place_(soundtrack)#cite_note-8) A vinyl edition of the soundtrack was released through [Mondo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mondo_(American_company) "Mondo (American company)") and Death Waltz Recording Company on July 11, 2018.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Quiet_Place_(soundtrack)#cite_note-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Quiet_Place_(soundtrack)#cite_note-10)

## Critical reception

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=A_Quiet_Place_(soundtrack)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Critical reception")]

Eric Kohn of _[IndieWire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IndieWire "IndieWire")_ wrote "Marco Beltrami's score largely sticks to a low rumble that hovers on the same wavelength as the characters' unease."[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Quiet_Place_(soundtrack)#cite_note-11) Sandy Schaefer of _[Screen Rant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Screen\_Rant "Screen Rant")_ wrote "Marco Beltrami's ominous score certainly help to set the mood throughout its runtime."[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Quiet_Place_(soundtrack)#cite_note-12) Tom Shone of _[The Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Times "The Times")_ described the score as "fussy and over-funereal".[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Quiet_Place_(soundtrack)#cite_note-13) Peter Travers of _[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling\_Stone "Rolling Stone")_ felt that "Only the score by Marco Beltrami seems too much, since _A Quiet Place_ works best when it sneaks up on you."[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Quiet_Place_(soundtrack)#cite_note-14)

_**A Quiet Place (Music from the Motion Picture)**_ is the [soundtrack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soundtrack "Soundtrack") to the [2018 film of the same name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Quiet_Place "A Quiet Place") directed by [John Krasinski](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Krasinski "John Krasinski"). Featuring musical score composed by [Marco Beltrami](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marco_Beltrami "Marco Beltrami"), the soundtrack was released under the [Milan Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milan_Records "Milan Records") label on April 6, 2018.

## Development

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=A_Quiet_Place_(soundtrack)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Development")]

Marco Beltrami had composed the musical score for _A Quiet Place_.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Quiet_Place_(soundtrack)#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Quiet_Place_(soundtrack)#cite_note-2) He signed the film over the occasion of [Thanksgiving](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thanksgiving_(United_States) "Thanksgiving (United States)") (November 23, 2017) and was set to compose the score by early-January 2018 in a short span of time while Beltrami was also scoring the [National Geographic Films](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Geographic_Films "National Geographic Films") documentary _[Free Solo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free\_Solo "Free Solo")_.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Quiet_Place_(soundtrack)#cite_note-:0-3) Due to the film's limited budget, Beltrami refrained from using a full-fledged orchestra for recording as "the film is truly intimate and contained". He used a small ensemble of 30 musicians which involved strings and piano and extensively manipulated and processed the score "so that we could create sounds that were semi-orchestral and semi-electronic".[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Quiet_Place_(soundtrack)#cite_note-4)

The initial blueprint for the original score came from Krasinski's passion for the cover version of [David Bowie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Bowie "David Bowie")'s "[Heroes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%22Heroes%22_(David_Bowie_song) "\"Heroes\" (David Bowie song)")" by [Peter Gabriel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Gabriel "Peter Gabriel"). Krasinski played the song to Beltrami while scoring the film and it became the basis of the score to Beltrami. He composed a family theme and sent to Krasinski which he liked it and eventually included into the edit. For the sound-hunting creatures, he wanted to come up with "a signature monster sound, something we haven't heard before that instills fear, even if the monster isn't onscreen".[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Quiet_Place_(soundtrack)#cite_note-:0-3) This resulted in the opening theme "It Hears You". Beltrami felt recording the final cue was difficult to him, as "when they realize that they can kill the monsters and the monsters are racing toward them, that cue was really crucial to the process [...] Once I solved that, everything else fell into place. It's not a melodic cue, but it's a driving force which led to the monster cue."[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Quiet_Place_(soundtrack)#cite_note-:0-3)

Most of the score had been excluded from the film, which Krasinski found impactful having the score dominated the scenes.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Quiet_Place_(soundtrack)#cite_note-IGN_18-5) Beltrami provided supervising sound editors [Erik Aadahl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erik_Aadahl "Erik Aadahl") and [Ethan Van der Ryn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethan_Van_der_Ryn "Ethan Van der Ryn") music to work in a way that would not interfere with the sound design throughout the film.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Quiet_Place_(soundtrack)#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Quiet_Place_(soundtrack)#cite_note-7)

## Release

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=A_Quiet_Place_(soundtrack)&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Release")]

The soundtrack to _A Quiet Place_ was released under the [Milan Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milan_Records "Milan Records") label on April 6, 2018.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Quiet_Place_(soundtrack)#cite_note-8) A vinyl edition of the soundtrack was released through [Mondo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mondo_(American_company) "Mondo (American company)") and Death Waltz Recording Company on July 11, 2018.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Quiet_Place_(soundtrack)#cite_note-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Quiet_Place_(soundtrack)#cite_note-10)

## Critical reception

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=A_Quiet_Place_(soundtrack)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Critical reception")]

Eric Kohn of _[IndieWire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IndieWire "IndieWire")_ wrote "Marco Beltrami's score largely sticks to a low rumble that hovers on the same wavelength as the characters' unease."[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Quiet_Place_(soundtrack)#cite_note-11) Sandy Schaefer of _[Screen Rant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Screen\_Rant "Screen Rant")_ wrote "Marco Beltrami's ominous score certainly help to set the mood throughout its runtime."[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Quiet_Place_(soundtrack)#cite_note-12) Tom Shone of _[The Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Times "The Times")_ described the score as "fussy and over-funereal".[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Quiet_Place_(soundtrack)#cite_note-13) Peter Travers of _[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling\_Stone "Rolling Stone")_ felt that "Only the score by Marco Beltrami seems too much, since _A Quiet Place_ works best when it sneaks up on you."[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Quiet_Place_(soundtrack)#cite_note-14)
